drivingQuestion: May a burial procession set out adjacent to the time for the recitation of Shema?
outcomeNote: The difficulty from Rav Yosef's funeral is answered by distinguishing the case of an important person.

segments.he: נוֹשְׂאֵי הַמִּטָּה וְחִלּוּפֵיהֶן. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַמֵּת סָמוּךְ לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. וְאִם הִתְחִילוּ — אֵין מַפְסִיקִין. אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב יוֹסֵף אַפְּקוּהוּ סָמוּךְ לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע! אָדָם חָשׁוּב שָׁאנֵי.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «the pallbearers and their replacements» are exempt from the recitation of Shema. On this subject, the Gemara cites that which the «Sages taught» in a baraita: «The deceased may not be taken out» to be buried «adjacent to» the time for «the recitation of Shema,» but should be buried later. «And if they» already «started» to take him out, «they need not stop» in order to recite Shema. The Gemara challenges: «Is that so? Didn’t they take Rav Yosef out» to be buried «adjacent to» the time for «the recitation of Shema?» The Gemara resolves this contradiction: The case of «an important person is different,» and they are more lenient in order to honor him at his burial.
